subject: Assurance sprint: access windows, scope carveouts, and contract flow
messages:
From: Charlotte Nguyen <charlotte.nguyen@medwell.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@medwell.com
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify audit rights and staging window for SOC2 / test access

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the kickoff yesterday. Legal here is reviewing the MSA + Order Form you sent and has a couple of asks on the security exhibit before we can get to signature. High level:

- We need clarity on the scope of audit rights (SOC 2 vs. full inspection). Our compliance team wants to avoid broad live-system inspections unless strictly scoped.
- Pen test notice: can you confirm the minimum notice and whether production access will ever be required for vendor-initiated tests?
- Evidence cadence: MedWell prefers monthly SOC artifact access for the first 90 days post go-live, then quarterly. Is that compatible?

Attached is our questionnaire (partial) for your security team; we flagged the items we think will drive redlines. Can someone from Redwood legal/security propose specific exhibit language and a suggested cadence that aligns with both parties?

Samir (copied) will be our contracting lead.

Best,
Charlotte
Charlotte Nguyen
Director, Compliance
MedWell Health

--- attachment: MedWell_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx (xlsx, 64 KB)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Charlotte Nguyen <charlotte.nguyen@medwell.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@medwell.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify audit rights and staging window for SOC2 / test access

Charlotte — thanks for the clear notes and the questionnaire. Looping in Laura (legal) and Karthik (security) to propose concrete language and an ops-friendly cadence. A few quick clarifications from my side so we don't talk past each other:

- Redwood's standard exhibit limits inspection to SOC 2 Type II evidence and onboarding windows; we typically provide sampling and encrypted artifact access rather than open live-system walkthroughs.
- For pen tests we ask for 30 days' notice, require an approved test plan, and prefer tests to run in staging unless customer explicitly requires production with a scoped blast radius and an agreed runbook.
- Evidence cadence: we can offer the monthly-for-90-days then quarterly model as an opt-in in the exhibit; I suspect we may need a short clause about ticketing SLAs for artifact requests.

Laura/Karthik — can you draft a short redline that: (1) defines "audit/inspection" as access to SOC2 reports and mutually agreed sampling, (2) sets pen-test notice and staging-first default, and (3) includes the proposed evidence cadence and a 3rd-party assessor carveout?

I can then send the redline back to Charlotte and Samir for review.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 09:10:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Clarify audit rights and staging window for SOC2 / test access

Marissa / team — draft redline attached. Key items I included (summary):

1) Narrowed definition of "Inspection/Audit":
   - Primary entitlement: access to Redwood's SOC 2 Type II reports, and exportable artifacts that correspond to the SOC 2 controls in scope.
   - Limited live inspections: permitted only for material compliance investigations and with 30 days' written notice; customer must provide a written justification and scope. On-site/interactive sessions are limited to 16 hours per 12-month period unless separately agreed.

2) Penetration testing:
   - Customer may request a pen test of Redwood-managed services with 30 days' notice.
   - Default execution environment is customer-specific staging/test environment. If customer requests production testing, both parties must agree in writing, and Redwood will require a scoped runbook and a hold-harmless/responsibility matrix.

3) Evidence cadence and ticketing:
   - For the first 90 days following go-live, Redwood will provide monthly artifact exports (where available) for SOC 2 controls. After 90 days, access will be quarterly.
   - Evidence requests will be routed via a shared ticket with an SLA of 5 business days for standard artifacts and 15 business days for deep-dive exports. Emergency requests may be escalated.

4) Third-party assessors / vendor access:
   - Assessors must be approved in advance and sign Redwood's standard NDA and AUP. Access tokens will be scoped and time-limited.

5) Redactions & Data minimization:
   - Redwood will provide redacted logs/artifacts where disclosure would expose other customers' data or platform internals; we included a short dispute-resolution path for contested redactions.

Attachments: Redwood_Security_Exhibit_Redline_v1.pdf (redline with inline comments).

Soojin — can you confirm the technical feasibility of the monthly export window and the SLA commitments? If we need to push any cadence language to "best-effort" rather than firm SLA, call it out so I can soften the contract language.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
--- attachment: Redwood_Security_Exhibit_Redline_v1.pdf (pdf, 120 KB)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: laojb@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 14:42:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Clarify audit rights and staging window for SOC2 / test access

Laura / Marissa — quick tech confirmation:

- Monthly exports: feasible if we limit scope to control-mapped artifacts (auth logs, config snapshots, change history). Generating full forensic exports on a monthly cadence for all controls will require additional ops time. Recommend we define a "standard artifact package" (list of artifacts) that is delivered monthly for 90 days; anything outside that package falls under the extended export SLA (15 business days).

- Pen tests: staging-first default is correct. For production tests, we need an agreed blast-radius doc, emergency rollback contact, and a mutually-signed runbook. Recommend adding a short acceptance gate: "Redwood to approve test plan and scope in writing before test commencement."

- Tokenized assessor access: we can provide ephemeral, scope-limited credentials with automatic expiry. We'll also require an IP allowlist and two-week window scheduling.

I'll add a short technical appendix to the redline that enumerates the "standard artifact package" and the ops steps to fulfill the SLA.

Karthik Iyer
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@medwell.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Charlotte Nguyen <charlotte.nguyen@medwell.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 15:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify audit rights and staging window for SOC2 / test access

Marissa / Laura / Karthik — thanks for the fast turnaround and the redline. We reviewed internally and MedWell can accept the proposed approach with the following tweaks:

- We agree to limit live inspections and prefer artifact exports, but would like the live-inspection cap increased to 24 hours per 12-month period (we can accept coordination constraints).
- For pen tests, 30 days' notice + staging-first is acceptable. For production tests (rare), we will provide a signed acceptance of the blast-radius and the runbook.
- Evidence cadence: monthly for 90 days then quarterly is fine. Please add a short note that emergency artifact requests (e.g., incident investigations) will be prioritized and handled under a separate incident response SLA.

If you can provide a clean redline (PDF) and a short cover note we will circulate to Legal Contracts and aim to return a countersigned order form within 7 business days.

Thanks —
Samir Patel
Sr. Contracts Manager, MedWell Health

--- Next steps: Marissa to attach clean redline and send with a 1-paragraph cover note to contracts@medwell.com
